source.title: DataComp: In search of the next generation of multimodal datasets
source.authors: S. Gadre; Gabriel Ilharco; Alex Fang; J. Hayase; G. Smyrnis; Thao Nguyen; Ryan Marten; Mitchell Wortsman; Dhruba Ghosh; Jieyu Zhang; E. Orgad; R. Entezari; G. Daras; Sarah Pratt; V. record.tranche_reason: The study tests downstream-performance trends across model/data scales using CLIP and image-text datasets, rather than measuring language-model held-out cross-entropy or fitting the original power laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own CLIP downstream evaluation results across scales, which bear on V6. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fit power laws, test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or test whether small-run loss fits predict larger-run loss. Its discussion of language-model scaling laws cites prior work rather than reporting tests of those laws.
record.test_reason: DataComp is a dataset-curation benchmark for CLIP, not a scaling-law study. Its four scales raise model size, samples seen, pool size and compute together. It fits no power law and does not test whether downstream performance can be predicted from scale or from pretraining loss. The rise in zero-shot accuracy across tiers is a byproduct of the benchmark's design. The cross-scale results are about whether rankings of filtering strategies stay the same across scales, a different construct from performance predictability. Kaplan and Hoffmann appear only as motivation and related work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is partly right but misses the main conclusions. The authors conclude that filtering a fixed pool, in particular more stringent filtering into smaller sets, beats training on the unfiltered pool at equal compute. DataComp-1B trains a ViT-L/14 to 79.2% ImageNet zero-shot, 3.7 pp above OpenAI CLIP at the same compute. Filtering-strategy rankings are largely consistent across scales, so small scales can guide dataset design. ImageNet is indicative of the average but not of every task. They make no claim about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image-text CLIP models and evaluates zero-shot classification/retrieval, rather than language models evaluated by held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It varies model architecture, training compute, and samples seen together; it does not fit the original loss laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Scale changes model architecture, training compute, and samples seen together. Downstream predictability also depends on the evaluation task: ImageNet performance is not consistently predictive for every individual dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Rankings of data-filtering strategies are largely preserved across compute scales: rank correlation 0.71–0.90 between scale pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative data-quality effects measured at small scale transfer to larger scale in CLIP training.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed samples seen, smaller CLIP-score-filtered subsets (~30% of the pool) beat the full unfiltered pool at every tier. Random subsets show larger is better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data quality shifts downstream performance at fixed compute independently of dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet accuracy correlates 0.99 with the 38-task average but correlates variably, sometimes negatively, with individual tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-benchmark proxies do not predict every downstream task.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
record.problems: The scale comparisons jointly vary training compute, training samples, and model architecture, so they do not isolate a single scaling variable. The study does not report held-out pretraining loss or fit loss-scaling laws. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported downstream scores.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports many additional filtering-strategy results in Tables 3 and 25–28 and BYOD results in Table 18, as well as other downstream metrics. These were omitted to keep the record focused on selected cross-scale downstream-performance series and the reported cross-scale rank correlations; the full omitted series are in those tables.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss, no power-law fit, no isolated variation of parameters, data or compute.
No fits on small runs extrapolated to larger runs.
No shape ablation at fixed parameter count. The ConvNeXt swap (Table 11) checks filter-ranking consistency, not loss.
CLIP is another modality, but the power-law form is never fitted.
No test of predicting downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss. Tiers bundle architecture, data and compute, and no trend is fitted.
No exponents or fitting choices studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed. Downstream accuracy rising across benchmark tiers, where architecture, data and compute all change, with no fitted trend and no prediction, does not test predictability. The cross-scale correlations concern dataset rankings, not performance. The only scaling-law content is citation-level (Kaplan, Hoffmann, Cherti et al.).

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss, power-law fit, or independent variation of parameters, tokens, and compute.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or fitted allocation exponents.
No comparison of loss at fixed parameter count across architecture shapes.
The study trains multimodal CLIP models but does not test whether the claimed power-law form holds in this modality or regime.
Tests downstream performance across bundled model/data/compute scales, not downstream prediction from pretraining loss or from isolated changes in scale.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or departures from a single power-law loss curve are studied.

rows.operation_detail: Comparison of ImageNet accuracy with performance on individual downstream datasets

conditions.value: individual datasets in the evaluation suite

rows.measure: Correlation between ImageNet accuracy and accuracy on individual downstream datasets
rows.value: Varies substantially; in some cases the correlation is negative.
rows.note: The authors state this qualitative result; exact per-dataset correlation coefficients are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Correlation between ImageNet accuracy and other individual tasks across models. This is a proxy-metric relation, not a relation to scale or pretraining loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average performance over the 38-dataset suite for the three selected filtering settings across DATACOMP scales
reader_labels.reason: Average performance rises across the reported scales for each selected setting (r1–r12); filtering-method rank correlations across scale pairs are positive and reported as 0.708 to 0.895 for ImageNet and 0.708 to 0.876 for the average metric (r13–r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Prediction from ImageNet accuracy to individual downstream tasks
reader_labels.reason: The reported relation to individual task performance varies substantially and is sometimes negative, although ImageNet accuracy correlates strongly with the average suite score (r19).
